attribution: CC Commander field-tested prompt library — adapted from Anthropic’s Claude Code prompt library

prompts.prompt: give me an overview of this codebase: architecture, key directories, and how the pieces connect
prompts.title: Get oriented in a new repository
prompts.why: describe what you want to know, not which files to read — Claude explores and summarizes how it fits together.
prompts.makeItStick: run `/init` to write a `CLAUDE.md` so Claude remembers this every session.

prompts.prompt: explain what src/scheduler/queue.ts does and how data flows through it. write it up as an HTML page with a diagram, then open it in my browser
prompts.title: Explain unfamiliar code
prompts.why: name the file and say what output format you want (diagram, bullets, whatever fits how you learn).
prompts.makeItStick: set an output style so Claude always explains in your preferred format.

prompts.prompt: where do we validate uploaded file types?
prompts.title: Find where something happens
prompts.why: search by behavior, not filename — works even when you don't know the file name or directory.

prompts.prompt: what would break if I deleted the retryWithBackoff helper?
prompts.title: Check what breaks before you delete
prompts.why: ask before you remove anything; the list of callers tells you whether it's a one-line cleanup or a coordinated change.

prompts.prompt: look through the commit history of internal/auth/session.go and summarize how it evolved and why
prompts.title: Trace how code evolved
prompts.why: point at commit history when the question is

prompts.prompt: which files would I need to touch to add a dark mode toggle to settings?
prompts.title: Scope a change before you start
prompts.why: size the work before committing it to a roadmap — the file list reveals one-component vs. cross-cutting.

prompts.prompt: I am a PM. walk me through what happens when a user clicks Export to PDF, from the UI down to the result
prompts.title: Ask the codebase a product question
prompts.why: state your role so the answer is pitched at the right level; Claude explains what the product actually does from source.

prompts.prompt: plan how to refactor the payment module to support multiple currencies. list the files you would change, but don't edit anything yet
prompts.title: Plan a multi-file change before touching code
prompts.why: "don't edit yet" separates exploration from changes so you see the approach first. Shift+Tab enters plan mode to make this the default.

prompts.prompt: I want to build per-workspace rate limits. interview me about implementation, UX, edge cases, and tradeoffs until we have covered everything, then write the spec to SPEC.md
prompts.title: Draft a spec by interview
prompts.why: ask to be interviewed instead of writing the spec yourself — Claude surfaces things you hadn't considered.
prompts.makeItStick: save your interview questions as a `/spec` skill.

prompts.prompt: read @meeting-notes.md and write up the action items, then create a Linear ticket for each with acceptance criteria
prompts.title: Turn a meeting into tickets
prompts.why: skip the transcription step — Claude pulls action items and writes them straight into your tracker via MCP.
prompts.makeItStick: save as a `/tickets` skill.

prompts.prompt: list the error states, empty states, and edge cases for the file upload flow that the design needs to cover
prompts.title: Map edge cases before building
prompts.why: ask for what's missing, not what's there — the states a happy-path design tends to skip.

prompts.prompt: here is a mockup. build a working prototype I can click through, matching the layout and states shown
prompts.title: Turn a mockup into a working prototype
prompts.why: a clickable prototype answers questions a static mockup can't — hand working code to engineering.

prompts.prompt: implement this design, then take a screenshot of the result, compare it to the original, and fix any differences
prompts.title: Implement from a screenshot and self-check
prompts.why: gives Claude a verification loop — it renders, compares, and iterates without you pointing out each gap.
prompts.makeItStick: use `/goal` to keep it iterating until the screenshots match.

prompts.prompt: look at how the GitHub webhook handler is implemented to understand the pattern, then build a Stripe webhook handler the same way
prompts.title: Follow an existing pattern
prompts.why: point at code you already like — without a reference Claude defaults to generic best practices; with one it matches your conventions.
prompts.makeItStick: have Claude write the pattern into `CLAUDE.md`.

prompts.prompt: find the public functions in src/auth/ without JSDoc comments and add them, matching the style already used in the file
prompts.title: Generate docs for undocumented code
prompts.why: name the scope and format; Claude matches the existing comment style.

prompts.prompt: add a /health endpoint that returns the app version and uptime
prompts.title: Add a small, well-defined feature
prompts.why: state inputs and outputs, not how to build it — Claude finds where similar code lives and adds yours alongside.

prompts.prompt: create a drag-and-drop Kanban board with three columns using HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript, then open it in my browser
prompts.title: Build a small internal tool from scratch
prompts.why: no project, framework, or build step needed — describe the tool and see it working immediately.

prompts.prompt: read issue #312, implement the fix, and run the tests
prompts.title: Work an issue end to end
prompts.why: give the issue number, not a summary — Claude reads the full ticket so requirements you'd forget come through, and it validates before reporting.

prompts.prompt: find every place we say "Sign up free" or a close variant, show me each one in context, then update them all to "Start free trial". leave tests and the changelog alone
prompts.title: Find and update copy across the codebase
prompts.why: ask for variants and say what to skip — catches phrasings a literal search misses, leaves fixtures/history alone.

prompts.prompt: read the privacy impact assessments in legal/pia/ to learn the structure and voice, then draft a new one for the new analytics integration
prompts.title: Draft a document from past examples
prompts.why: point at a folder of finished work instead of describing your style — the first draft reads like one of yours.
prompts.makeItStick: save the voice as a skill.

prompts.prompt: write tests for app/parsers/feed.py, run them, and fix any failures
prompts.title: Write tests, run them, fix failures
prompts.why: ask for write + run + fix together so Claude iterates without stopping for instructions.
prompts.makeItStick: run `/init` so Claude learns your test command.

prompts.prompt: write tests for the password reset flow first, then implement it until they pass
prompts.title: Drive implementation from tests
prompts.why: TDD — the tests define "done" and Claude iterates until they pass.

prompts.prompt: read coverage/coverage-summary.json and add tests for the lowest-covered files until each is above 80%
prompts.title: Fill gaps from a coverage report
prompts.why: point at the actual coverage numbers instead of guessing what's untested.
prompts.makeItStick: set as a `/goal` so it keeps writing tests until coverage hits the target.

prompts.prompt: migrate everything from the old logging API to the structured logger: identify every place that needs to change, then make the changes
prompts.title: Migrate a pattern across the codebase
prompts.why: describe old → new and ask Claude to identify every call site first, so nothing is missed.

prompts.prompt: port this Python module to Rust, keeping the same public API and test behavior
prompts.title: Port code to another language
prompts.why: say what to preserve, not just the target language — naming the contract gives Claude something to check the port against.

prompts.prompt: optimize the search query to bring p95 latency from 2s down to under 500ms
prompts.title: Optimize against a measurable target
prompts.why: stating metric + target gives a clear definition of done.
prompts.makeItStick: set as a `/goal` so it keeps measuring until it hits the number.

prompts.prompt: the login button extends 20px beyond the card border on mobile. fix it.
prompts.title: Fix a precise visual bug
prompts.why: precise visual feedback (element, measurement, viewport) gets a precise fix.
prompts.makeItStick: add a preview tool so Claude screenshots and verifies.

prompts.prompt: review my uncommitted changes and flag anything that looks risky before I commit
prompts.title: Review your changes before you commit
prompts.why: Claude reads the changed files in full, not just diff lines, so it spots issues a quick self-review misses.
prompts.makeItStick: run `/code-review` for the same check in one command.

prompts.prompt: review PR #247 and summarize what changed, then list any concerns
prompts.title: Review a pull request
prompts.why: Claude reviews with the whole codebase in context, not just the diff.
prompts.makeItStick: turn on Code Review for every PR.

prompts.prompt: what is this going to do, and is anything here going to cause problems?
prompts.context: paste your Terraform plan output, then:
prompts.title: Review infrastructure changes before applying
prompts.why: plan output is dense — pasting it gets a plain-language summary before you apply.

prompts.prompt: use a subagent to review src/api/ for security issues and report what it finds
prompts.title: Run a security review with a subagent
prompts.why: a subagent runs the audit in its own context and reports a summary, so a long review doesn't fill your main session.
prompts.makeItStick: set up a dedicated security-review subagent.

prompts.prompt: review launch-post.md for unsupported claims, missing attributions, and brand-guideline issues and list anything I should fix before it goes to legal
prompts.title: Catch issues before formal review
prompts.why: get a focused first pass before a human spends time on it.
prompts.makeItStick: capture your review checklist as a team skill.

prompts.prompt: that is not right: the function signature needs to stay backward-compatible. try a different approach
prompts.title: Course-correct a wrong approach
prompts.why: name the constraint Claude missed, not just that it's wrong — a specific reason beats "guess again."
prompts.makeItStick: `Esc Esc` to rewind code + conversation so the retry starts clean.

prompts.prompt: that is too much. keep only the changes to the validation logic in src/forms/ and undo your other edits
prompts.title: Narrow the scope of a change
prompts.why: when the direction is right but the change went too broad, keep part of it instead of rewinding everything.

prompts.prompt: you keep using default exports when this project uses named exports. add a rule to CLAUDE.md so this stops happening
prompts.title: Turn a correction into a rule
prompts.why: a chat correction isn't shared; a `CLAUDE.md` rule is read at the start of every session (and shared once committed).
prompts.makeItStick: open `/memory` to review what Claude wrote.

prompts.prompt: resolve the merge conflicts in this branch and explain what you kept from each side
prompts.title: Resolve merge conflicts
prompts.why: say what state you want, not which markers to keep — asking for the reasoning makes the merge reviewable.

prompts.prompt: commit these changes with a message that summarizes what I did
prompts.title: Commit with a generated message
prompts.why: Claude derives the message from the diff and matches your repo's existing commit style.

prompts.prompt: find the Linear ticket about the login timeout and open a PR that implements it
prompts.title: Open a pull request from a ticket
prompts.why: one prompt reads the spec, makes the change, and opens the PR — no context switch between tracker, editor, and GitHub.

prompts.prompt: compare v2.3.0 to v2.4.0 and draft release notes grouped by feature, fix, and breaking change
prompts.title: Draft release notes from git history
prompts.why: give two reference points and the structure — Claude reads the commit log between them.
prompts.makeItStick: save as a `/changelog` skill.

prompts.prompt: write a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the tests and deploys to staging on every push to main
prompts.title: Write a CI workflow
prompts.why: describe when it runs and what it does; the YAML is generated, matched to your build/test commands.

prompts.prompt: the UserAuth test is failing, find out why and fix it
prompts.title: Find and fix a failing test
prompts.why: describe the symptom — you don't need to know which file is broken; Claude runs the test, traces into source, and fixes.

prompts.prompt: users are seeing 500 errors on /api/settings. investigate and tell me what is going on
prompts.title: Investigate a reported error
prompts.why: describe symptom + location; Claude reads the relevant path and traces likely causes.
prompts.makeItStick: put a deeplink in your runbook that opens Claude with this pre-filled.

prompts.prompt: fix the root cause and verify the build succeeds
prompts.title: Fix a build error at the root
prompts.why: asking for root cause + verification prevents surface patches that just suppress the error.

prompts.prompt: the checkout endpoint started returning 500s an hour ago. check the logs, recent deploys, and config changes, then tell me the most likely cause
prompts.title: Investigate a production incident
prompts.why: list the evidence sources to correlate, not the steps to take — Claude reads logs, git history, and config together.
prompts.makeItStick: connect Sentry/log store via MCP.

prompts.prompt: walk me through why this pod is failing and give me the exact commands to fix it
prompts.context: paste a screenshot of the console, then:
prompts.title: Diagnose from a console screenshot
prompts.why: cloud consoles show the problem but not the fix — Claude translates the dashboard into kubectl/gcloud/aws commands.

prompts.prompt: show me all failed logins for the auth service over the past 24 hours. write the query, run it, and tell me what stands out
prompts.title: Query logs in plain English
prompts.why: ask the question instead of writing SQL — Claude builds the query, runs it, and shows both query and result.

prompts.prompt: read @reports/q1-signups.csv, summarize the key patterns, and write the results to an HTML page with charts, then open it in my browser
prompts.title: Analyze a data file
prompts.why: a one-off question doesn't need a one-off script — point at a file and Claude reads it directly.
prompts.makeItStick: connect the data source via MCP instead of exporting files.

prompts.prompt: read @ads-performance.csv, find the underperforming headlines, and generate 20 new variations that stay under 90 characters
prompts.title: Generate variations from performance data
prompts.why: state the constraint up front so generation stays within the limit.
prompts.makeItStick: connect the ad platform via MCP.

prompts.prompt: create a /ship skill for this project that runs the linter and tests, then drafts a commit message
prompts.title: Turn a recurring task into a skill
prompts.why: name the steps once, reuse them as a command — Claude writes a skill anyone on your team can run.

prompts.prompt: write a hook that runs prettier after every edit to a .ts or .tsx file
prompts.title: Add a hook for repeat behavior
prompts.why: hooks make a behavior automatic instead of something you must remember to ask for.

prompts.prompt: set up the Sentry MCP server so you can read my error reports directly
prompts.title: Connect a tool with MCP
prompts.why: connect the source once instead of pasting data every session.

prompts.prompt: summarize what we did this session and suggest what to add to CLAUDE.md
prompts.title: Capture what to remember for next time
prompts.why: Claude knows what it had to figure out this session and proposes `CLAUDE.md` entries so the next session starts with that context.

patterns.title: Describe the outcome, not the steps.
patterns.why: Say what you want; let Claude find the files.
patterns.example: add rate limiting to the public API and make sure existing tests still pass

patterns.title: Give it a way to check its own work.
patterns.why: Ask for run/test/compare/verify in the same prompt so it iterates instead of stopping.
patterns.example: write the migration, run it against the dev database, and confirm the schema matches

patterns.title: Point at a reference.
patterns.why: Name an existing file/test/pattern to match.
patterns.example: add a settings page that follows the same layout as the profile page

patterns.title: State the measurable target.
patterns.why: Give the metric and threshold so "done" is unambiguous.
patterns.example: get the bundle size under 200KB and show me what you removed

patterns.title: Give it the artifact.
patterns.why: Paste errors/logs/screenshots or `@`-mention files instead of describing them.

patterns.title: Say how you want the answer.
patterns.example: explain how the payment retry logic works as an HTML page with a diagram, then open it in my browser

modules.objective: write prompts that need fewer corrections.
